the choice of data reduction method is highly application dependent.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how to efficiently process and analyze multivariate time series data in sensor networks.
the problem of reducing the data generated by sensor nodes in a sensor network to a manageable level.
the development of methods to analyze and process data streams generated by sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no best method to reduce multivariate stream data in sensor network applications, and that the choice of a method should depend on the type of application and data.
the Wavelet-based method is the best choice in terms of data quality, data reduction rate and the amount of data to be stored in the network.
the Wavelet-based methods are the best for the reduction of real data streams, while the sampling method is the best for the synthetic data streams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SVD method is the best reduction method for the sensor network applications that require the reconstruction of the data at the base station.
the reduction techniques are useful in sensor network applications and can provide significant reduction rates.
the SVD method performs better than other techniques in most applications, and the sampling method is the least efficient in most cases.

the choice of the reduction technique should be application dependent, as different applications have different requirements.
the choice of a reduction technique depends on the application and the type of data generated by the sensors.
